final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic Schiff-base lysine that covalently anchors the PLP cofactor; substituting it directly abolishes cofactor attachment and catalysis, the most reliable loss-of-function change.
Located in the conserved TSGNTG PLP/substrate-binding loop; disrupting this motif should strongly impair substrate positioning and activity.
Glycine in the same catalytic TSGNTG loop; introducing a bulky charged Arg is expected to sterically and electrostatically distort the active-site conformation.

stop_reason.detail: No evidence tools are available and the top candidates rest on strong mechanistic reasoning that self-iteration cannot further validate.

history.rationale: Lys119 forms the Schiff base with the PLP cofactor (catalytic lysine in the TSGN...PLP-binding motif region); removing this residue eliminates cofactor attachment and abolishes catalysis.
K119 is the catalytic PLP-binding Schiff-base lysine in CBS; removing it directly abolishes cofactor attachment and catalysis, making this the most reliable LoF mutation.
Threonine in the TSGN active-site loop contributes to substrate/cofactor positioning; loss of the hydroxyl could impair catalysis.
Sits within the conserved TSGNTG PLP/substrate-binding motif (TSGNTGIG, ~res 258-265), so disrupting it should strongly impair activity.
Glycine in the flexible PLP-binding loop (TSGNTG motif) is conformationally required; a bulky charged Arg would sterically block cofactor accommodation.
Glycine substitutions to bulky Arg in conserved catalytic-domain regions are known destabilizing pathogenic-type changes; kept as strong backup.
Arg266 is a known catalytically/structurally important residue in CBS; neutralizing this charge disrupts active-site electrostatics and substrate binding.
Adjacent to the TSGNTG motif and likely participates in substrate/PLP positioning, but Ala substitution may be tolerated more than backbone-disrupting changes.
Conserved glycine within the second catalytic/dimerization region; substitution with bulky Arg likely destabilizes the fold and disrupts activity.
Conserved Gly-to-Arg in the core is plausibly disruptive but its precise catalytic role is less certain than the PLP-motif residues.
Asparagine in the PLP-binding loop hydrogen bonds to the cofactor phosphate; removal weakens PLP retention and lowers activity.
Near the catalytic domain but single Ala mutations of Asn are often only partially impairing.
Charge reversal of an active-site acidic residue could disrupt the electrostatic network required for catalysis.
Charge-reversal could disturb electrostatics but effect magnitude is uncertain without evidence.
Glycine in the conserved GTGGT motif is essential for backbone flexibility; a large charged residue would sterically abolish proper folding of the catalytic loop.
Glycine in the same TSGNTG catalytic loop; a bulky charged Arg would sterically and electrostatically disrupt the active-site loop conformation.
Proline substitution in a catalytic-region backbone would rigidify/kink the chain, likely disrupting active-site geometry and function.
Proline can break secondary structure and destabilize the fold, giving indirect LoF, but positional impact is speculative.
